title: A SpiderPR submit is an async paid distribution: 201 = queued, not published; the URL comes later and a re-submit is a SECOND charge
summary: POST /jobs/spiderPR/submit enqueues a wire-distribution job and returns a job_id with status 'queued' — it does NOT return a published_url. The release is rendered and submitted to the provider by a poll worker seconds-to-minutes later, then reaches 'published'. Reporting 'here's your link' off the 201 surfaces a URL that does not exist yet; poll getJobStatus until completed/failed, then read published_url + wire_report_url from getJobResults. There is no idempotency key, so a retried submit sends AND bills a second distribution — submit once, and if a prior submit 'looks stuck', poll its job_id rather than re-POSTing. A failed job is not retryable in place: its reason is in getJobResults.error; fix the copy and submit a NEW release.
references: app/schemas/spider_pr.py (SpiderPRJobSubmit wraps the release under `payload`; SpiderPRData carries status/published_url/wire_report_url/error)
SpiderPR World-B 1.1 (PR #2875, migration 467) — spiderPR job type + PostgreSQL job_queue dispatch
Analog: spidermail learnings/2026-06-10-queued-is-not-sent (async job, 201=queued, no idempotency key)
